text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Histadrut leader Amir Peretz meet; end to one-day strike.
- Swiss list includes Nazi, war profiteers. List is anticlimactic.
- European Union hopes to ease Golan Heights vote flap.
- Treasury predicts 7.7 percent jobless rate by year's end.
- Government: Antitrust hitch with Claridge-Koor deal.
- Treasury: Privatisation proceeds will pay debts.
GLOBES
- Treasury: Unemployment could soar to 11.5 percent record in the year 2000.
- Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman: We'll continue privatising despite the strikes.
HAARETZ
- Jerusalem municipality approves Jewish neighbourhood in Ras al-Amoud.
- U.S. effort concentrates on formula for freezing Jewish settlements. Netanyahu opposes it.
- Thousands have already turned to accountants dealing with financial claims on Swiss accounts from before World War Two.
MAARIV
- Light arms fire directed at deputy army chief's helicopter over Palestinian-ruled Bethlehem late at night.
- Double sovereignty in East Jerusalem part of draft plan in prime minister's office. Report is denied.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Fury in Netanyahu's office: "Jordan's King Hussein is boycotting us".
